summary: Boolean module arguments accept many case-insensitive values: true/false, yes/no, on/off, t/f, y/n, 1/0 and 1.0/0.0; docs use true/false for ansible-lint compatibility.
questions: Can I use yes/no for boolean module options?
What values count as true in Ansible module arguments?
Is 'on' a valid boolean in Ansible?

answer_card.title: Valid boolean values
answer_card.answer_md:
Case-insensitive.
- **Truthy:** `True`, `'true'`, `'t'`, `'yes'`, `'y'`, `'on'`, `'1'`, `1`, `1.0`
- **Falsy:** `False`, `'false'`, `'f'`, `'no'`, `'n'`, `'off'`, `'0'`, `0`, `0.0`

Docs use `true`/`false` to match ansible-lint defaults.
